title: Make 10: Find the Number That Makes 10
seo_title: Kindergarten Make 10 Worksheets: Ten-Frames, Pairs That Make 10, How Many More
standard_text: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten make 10 worksheets: fill a ten-frame, find the missing part (7 + ? = 10), find how many are hidden, learn the pairs that make 10, and solve how-many-more stories. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count the empty boxes in a ten-frame. They show how many more make 10.
key_sub: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5 make 10.
body_html:
Make 10 with a ten-frame

A ten-frame has 10 boxes. Count the dots. The empty boxes show how many more make 10.

Pairs that make 10

NumberGoes withSentence
191 + 9 = 10
282 + 8 = 10
373 + 7 = 10
464 + 6 = 10
555 + 5 = 10
646 + 4 = 10
737 + 3 = 10
828 + 2 = 10
919 + 1 = 10

Count on to 10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Answering with the number you seeFind how many more make 10
Counting the start when counting onStart after the number: 7, 8, 9, 10
Off by oneCount the empty boxes

faq.a: Our numbers are built on tens. Children who know 7 and 3 make 10 can later add 8 + 5 by making a 10 first (8 + 2 + 3). It is the base for adding and subtracting to 20.

faq.q: How can I practice making 10 at home?
faq.a: Use 10 fingers: hold up 6 and ask how many are down. Use an egg carton with 10 cups, or hide some of 10 toys under a cup and ask how many are hidden.
1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, and 5 and 5. The order does not matter: 3 + 7 and 7 + 3 both make 10.

faq.q: Should kindergartners know these by heart?
faq.a: By the end of kindergarten, children should find the partner for any number 1 to 9, using objects, drawings or ten-frames. Quick recall builds over time in Grade 1.
